/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Most logging workers have a high school diploma. They get on-the-job training to become familiar with forest environments and to learn how to operate logging machinery.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Logging is physically demanding and can be dangerous. Workers spend all their time outdoors, sometimes in poor weather and often in isolated areas.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: logging workers.    Conservation scientists and foresters manage the land quality of forests, parks, rangelands, and other natural resources. Construction equipment operators drive, maneuver, or control the heavy machinery used to construct roads, buildings, and other structures. Forest and conservation workers perform physical labor to improve the quality of natural areas such as forests, rangelands, and wetlands.

/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Logisticians typically need a bachelor’s degree to enter the occupation. Employers often prefer to hire candidates who have experience in a related occupation. In some cases, work experience may substitute for education.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Logisticians work in many industries. Most work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: logisticians. Industrial engineers design, develop, and test integrated systems for managing industrial production processes. Industrial production managers oversee the operations of manufacturing and related plants. Management analysts recommend ways to improve an organization’s efficiency. Operations research analysts use mathematics and logic to help solve complex issues. Quality control inspectors examine products and materials for defects or deviations from specifications. Buyers and purchasing agents buy products and services for organizations. Purchasing managers oversee the work of buyers and purchasing agents. Meeting, convention, and event planners arrange all aspects of events and professional gatherings. Project management specialists coordinate the budget, schedule, staffing, and other details of a project.

/occupation/occupation_name_short_singul: Machinist or Tool and Die Maker
/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Machinists and tool and die makers set up and operate a variety of computer-controlled and mechanically controlled equipment to produce precision metal parts, instruments, and tools.  Read detailed drawings or files, such as blueprints, sketches, and those for computer-aided design (CAD) and computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) Machinists
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Although machinists typically need a high school diploma to enter the occupation, tool and die makers also may need to complete postsecondary courses. Machinists and tool and die makers typically are trained on the job. Some learn through training or apprenticeship programs, vocational schools, or community and technical colleges.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Machinists and tool and die makers work in machine shops and factories. Many work full time during regular business hours. However, working overtime, as well as nights and weekends, may be common.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: machinists and tool and die makers. Welders, cutters, solderers, and brazers use hand-held or remotely controlled equipment to join, repair, or cut metal parts and products.

Gather and organize information about the problems to be solved or the procedures to be improved management consultants
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Management analysts typically need at least a bachelor’s degree and several years of related work experience.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Management analysts may travel frequently to meet with clients. Some work more than 40 hours per week.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: management analysts.    Accountants and auditors prepare and examine financial records. Market research analysts study consumer preferences, business conditions, and other factors to assess potential sales of a product or service. Operations research analysts use mathematics and logic to help solve complex issues. Project management specialists coordinate the budget, schedule, staffing, and other details of a project.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Manicurists and pedicurists clean, shape, and beautify fingernails and toenails.  Discuss nail treatments and services available nail technicians
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Manicurists and pedicurists must complete a state-approved cosmetology or nail technician program and then pass a state exam for licensure.   Business skills
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Manicurists and pedicurists usually work in a nail salon, spa, or hair salon. Most manicurists and pedicurists work full time, although part-time work is common. Work schedules may vary and often include evenings and weekends.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: manicurists and pedicurists.    Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists provide haircutting, hairstyling, and other services related to personal appearance. Skincare specialists provide cleansing and other face and body treatments to enhance a person’s appearance.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Marine engineers and naval architects design, develop, and evaluate the operation of marine vessels, ship machinery, and related equipment, such as power supply and propulsion systems.  Study design proposals and specifications to establish basic characteristics of a marine vessel, such as its size, weight, and speed
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Marine engineers and naval architects typically need a bachelor’s degree in marine engineering, naval architecture, or a related field. Some marine engineering and naval architecture programs are offered at state maritime academies.   Attention to detail.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Marine engineers and naval architects may work in a variety of settings, such as in offices, on manufacturing shop floors, or at sea. Most marine engineers and naval architects work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week.

Water transportation workers operate and maintain vessels that take cargo and people over water.

Social and human service assistants provide client services in a variety of fields, such as psychology, rehabilitation, and social work. Genetic counselors assess clients' risk for a variety of inherited conditions, such as birth defects.

/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Massage therapists typically complete a postsecondary education program that combines study and experience, although standards and requirements vary by state. /occupation/summary_work_environment: Massage therapists work in an array of settings, such as spas and offices of other health practitioners. For example, some operators move goods around factories and storage areas or onto container ships. Others move construction materials around building sites.  Set up and inspect material moving equipment Conveyor operators and tenders
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Education and training requirements vary by occupation. Crane operators typically have several years of experience in a related occupation.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most material moving machine operators work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week. Because materials are shipped around the clock, some operators work overnight shifts.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: material moving machine operators.    Construction equipment operators drive, maneuver, or control the heavy machinery used to construct roads, buildings, and other structures. Delivery truck drivers and driver/sales workers pick up, transport, and drop off packages and small shipments within a local region or urban area. Hand laborers and material movers manually move freight, stock, or other materials. Heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers transport goods from one location to another. Railroad workers ensure that passenger and freight trains operate safely. They may drive trains, coordinate the activities of the trains, or control signals and switches in the rail yard. Water transportation workers operate and maintain vessels that take cargo and people over water.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Material recording clerks track product information in order to keep businesses and supply chains on schedule. They ensure proper scheduling, recordkeeping, and inventory control.  Keep records of items shipped, received, or transferred to another location Production, planning, and expediting clerks
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Material recording clerks typically need a high school diploma or equivalent and are trained on the job.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most material recording clerks work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: material recording clerks.    General office clerks perform a variety of clerical tasks, including answering telephones, typing documents, and filing records. Hand laborers and material movers manually move freight, stock, or other materials. Information clerks perform routine clerical duties, maintain records, collect data, and provide information to customers.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Materials engineers develop, process, and test materials used to create a range of products, from computer chips and aircraft wings to golf clubs and biomedical devices. They study the properties and structures of metals, ceramics, plastics, composites, nanomaterials (extremely small substances), and other substances in order to create new materials that meet certain mechanical, electrical, and chemical requirements. They also help select materials for specific products and develop new ways to use existing materials.  Plan and evaluate new projects, consulting with other engineers and managers as necessary Ceramic engineers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Materials engineers typically need a bachelor’s degree in materials science and engineering or in a related engineering field. Completing internships and cooperative-engineering programs while in school may be helpful for gaining hands-on experience.  A degree from an ABET-accredited engineering program Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Materials engineers generally work in offices where they have access to computers and design equipment. Others work in factories or research and development laboratories. Materials engineers typically work full time and may work overtime hours when necessary.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: materials engineers.    Aerospace engineers design, develop, and test aircraft, spacecraft, satellites, and missiles. Architectural and engineering managers plan, direct, and coordinate activities in the fields of architecture and engineering. Bioengineers and biomedical engineers combine engineering principles with sciences to design and create equipment, devices, computer systems, and software. Calibration technologists and technicians inspect, adjust, and test measurement devices against standards, such as those used in manufacturing, healthcare, and other industries. Chemical engineers apply the principles of chemistry, physics, and engineering to design equipment and processes for manufacturing products such as gasoline, detergents, and paper. Chemists and materials scientists research and analyze the chemical properties of substances to develop new materials, products, or knowledge. Electrical engineers design, develop, test, and supervise the manufacture of electrical equipment. Mechanical engineers design, develop, build, and test mechanical and thermal sensors and devices. Physicists and astronomers study the interactions of matter and energy. Sales engineers sell business products or services, such as software or support, that require technical expertise.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Mathematicians and statisticians analyze data and apply computational techniques to solve problems.  Decide what data are needed to answer specific questions or problems Colleges and universities.
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Mathematicians and statisticians typically need at least a master’s degree in mathematics or statistics. However, some positions are available to those with a bachelor’s degree.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: The top employers of mathematicians and statisticians are the federal government and scientific research and development companies. Mathematicians and statisticians may work on teams with engineers, scientists, and other specialists.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: mathematicians and statisticians.    Actuaries use mathematics, statistics, and financial theory to analyze the economic costs of risk and uncertainty. Computer systems analysts study an organization’s current computer systems and design ways to improve efficiency. Data scientists use analytical tools and techniques to extract meaningful insights from data. Financial analysts guide businesses and individuals in decisions about expending money to attain profit. Market research analysts study consumer preferences, business conditions, and other factors to assess potential sales of a product or service. Operations research analysts use mathematics and logic to help solve complex issues. Postsecondary teachers instruct students in a variety of academic subjects beyond the high school level. Survey researchers design and conduct surveys and analyze data. Economists conduct research, prepare reports, and evaluate issues related to monetary and fiscal policy. They also may collect and analyze statistical data. Computer programmers write, modify, and test code and scripts that allow computer software and applications to function properly. Physicists and astronomers study the interactions of matter and energy.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Mechanical engineering technologists and technicians help mechanical engineers design, develop, test, and manufacture tools, engines, machines, and other devices. They may make sketches and rough layouts, record and analyze data, and report their findings.  Evaluate specifications in design drawings prior to adding or replacing tools
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Mechanical engineering technologists and technicians typically need an associate’s degree or other postsecondary training to enter the occupation.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Mechanical engineering technologists and technicians work primarily in factories or in research and development labs. Most work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: mechanical engineering technologists and technicians.    Calibration technologists and technicians inspect, adjust, and test measurement devices against standards, such as those used in manufacturing, healthcare, and other industries. Drafters use software to convert the designs of engineers and architects into technical drawings. Industrial engineering technologists and technicians help engineers solve problems affecting manufacturing layout or production. Machinists and tool and die makers set up and operate equipment to produce precision metal parts, instruments, and tools. Mechanical engineers design, develop, build, and test mechanical and thermal sensors and devices.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Mechanical engineers research, design, develop, build, and test mechanical and thermal sensors and devices, including tools, engines, and machines.  Analyze problems to see how mechanical and thermal devices might help solve a particular problem Auto research engineers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Mechanical engineers typically need a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or mechanical engineering technology. Mechanical engineers who sell services publicly must be licensed in all states and the District of Columbia.  A degree from an ABET-accredited engineering program Creativity.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Mechanical engineers generally work in offices. They may occasionally visit worksites where a problem or piece of equipment needs their personal attention. Mechanical engineers work mostly in engineering services, research and development, and manufacturing.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: mechanical engineers.    Drafters use software to convert the designs of engineers and architects into technical drawings. Materials engineers develop, process, and test materials used to create a wide range of products. Mathematicians and statisticians analyze data and apply computational techniques to solve problems. Mechanical engineering technologists and technicians help mechanical engineers design, develop, test, and manufacture machines and other devices. Natural sciences managers plan, supervise, or coordinate research and other activities in fields such as life sciences, physical sciences, mathematics, and statistics. Petroleum engineers devise methods to improve oil and gas extraction and production. Physicists and astronomers study the interactions of matter and energy. Sales engineers sell business products or services, such as software or support, that require technical expertise. Nuclear engineers research and develop projects or address problems concerning the release, control, and use of nuclear energy and nuclear waste disposal.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Medical and health services managers, also called healthcare executives or healthcare administrators, plan, direct, and coordinate medical and health services. They may manage an entire facility, a specific clinical area or department, or a medical practice for a group of physicians. Medical and health services managers must adapt to changes in healthcare laws, regulations, and technology.  Develop goals and objectives related to efficiency and quality of healthcare services healthcare executives
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Medical and health services managers typically need a bachelor’s degree to enter the occupation; however, educational requirements vary by facility and specific function. Prospective managers also typically need work experience in an administrative or clinical role in a hospital or other healthcare facility.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most medical and health services managers work in healthcare facilities, including hospitals and nursing homes, and group medical practices. Most work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: medical and health services managers.    Administrative services and facilities managers plan, direct, and coordinate activities that help an organization run efficiently. Computer and information systems managers plan, coordinate, and direct computer-related activities in an organization. Financial managers create financial reports, direct investment activities, and develop plans for the long-term financial goals of their organization. Health information technologists and medical registrars advise organizations on computerized healthcare systems and analyze clinical data. Human resources managers plan, coordinate, and direct the administrative functions of an organization. Medical records specialists compile, process, and maintain patient files. Buyers and purchasing agents buy products and services for organizations. Purchasing managers oversee the work of buyers and purchasing agents. Registered nurses (RNs) provide and coordinate patient care and educate patients and the public about various health conditions. Social and community service managers coordinate and supervise programs and organizations that support public well-being. Top executives plan strategies and policies to ensure that an organization meets its goals.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Medical assistants complete administrative and clinical tasks, such as scheduling appointments and taking patients’ vital signs. Their duties vary by location, specialty, and employer.  Interview patients and record their medical history
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Medical assistants typically need postsecondary education, such as a certificate. Some workers enter the occupation with a high school diploma and learn through on-the-job training.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most medical assistants work full time. They are employed in physicians’ offices, hospitals, outpatient clinics, and other healthcare facilities.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: medical assistants.    Dental assistants provide patient care, take x rays, keep records, and schedule appointments. Dental hygienists examine patients for signs of oral diseases, such as gingivitis, and provide preventive care, including oral hygiene. Health information technologists and medical registrars advise organizations on computerized healthcare systems and analyze clinical data. Licensed practical nurses (LPNs) and licensed vocational nurses (LVNs) provide basic medical care. Medical records specialists compile, process, and maintain patient files. Nursing assistants provide basic care and help patients with activities of daily living. Orderlies transport patients and clean treatment areas. Occupational therapy assistants and aides help occupational therapists provide treatments and procedures to clients, or they do routine tasks such as preparing treatment rooms. Pharmacy technicians help pharmacists dispense prescription medication to customers or health professionals. Phlebotomists draw blood for tests, transfusions, research, or blood donations. Physical therapist assistants and aides are supervised by physical therapists to help patients regain movement and manage pain after injuries and illnesses. Psychiatric technicians and aides care for people who have mental conditions or developmental disabilities.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Medical dosimetrists calculate doses of radiation and design and oversee treatment plans for patients with cancer and other serious diseases.  Review a patient’s documents, such as their CT and MRI scans
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: To enter the occupation, medical dosimetrists typically need a bachelor's degree and must complete an accredited medical dosimetry program. Employers usually require workers to have certification.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most medical dosimetrists work in healthcare settings, such as hospitals and physicians' offices. They may spend much of their time working at a computer.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: medical dosimetrists.    Nuclear medicine technologists prepare and administer radioactive drugs for imaging or treatment. Physicians and surgeons diagnose and treat injuries or illnesses and address health maintenance. Physicists and astronomers study the interactions of matter and energy. Radiation therapists administer doses of radiation to patients who have cancer or other serious diseases. Radiologic technologists perform diagnostic imaging examinations on patients. MRI technologists operate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanners to create diagnostic images. Registered nurses (RNs) provide and coordinate patient care and educate patients and the public about various health conditions.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Medical equipment repairers install, maintain, and repair patient care equipment.  Install medical equipment biomedical equipment technicians
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Employers generally prefer candidates who have an associate’s degree in biomedical technology or engineering. Depending on the area of specialization, repairers may need a bachelor’s degree, especially for advancement.   Communication skills
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Although medical equipment repairers usually work during the day, they are sometimes expected to be on call, including evenings and weekends. Because repairing vital medical equipment is urgent, the work is sometimes stressful. Those who work in a patient-caring environment are potentially exposed to germs, diseases, and other health risks.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: medical equipment repairers.    Aircraft and avionics equipment mechanics and technicians install, test, adjust, and repair equipment and systems in aircraft. General maintenance and repair workers fix and maintain machines, mechanical equipment, and buildings. Industrial machinery mechanics, machinery maintenance workers, and millwrights install, maintain, and repair factory equipment and other industrial machinery. Clinical laboratory technologists and technicians perform medical laboratory tests for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease. Dental and ophthalmic laboratory technicians and medical appliance technicians make or repair dentures, eyeglasses, prosthetics, and related products.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Medical records specialists compile, process, and maintain patient files. They also may classify and enter patients’ medical information into the healthcare industry's numerical coding system.  Review patients’ records for timeliness, completeness, and accuracy Medical coders
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Medical records specialists typically need a postsecondary certificate to enter the occupation, although some qualify with a high school diploma. Others might need an associate’s degree. Certification may be required or preferred.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Medical records specialists typically spend many hours at a computer. Most work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: medical records specialists.    Health information technologists and medical registrars advise organizations on computerized healthcare systems and analyze clinical data. Information clerks perform routine clerical duties, maintain records, collect data, and provide information to customers.  Medical assistants complete administrative and clinical tasks, such as scheduling appointments and taking patients’ vital signs. Medical transcriptionists use electronic devices to convert voice recordings from physicians and other healthcare workers into formal reports. Pharmacy technicians help pharmacists dispense prescription medication to customers or health professionals.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Medical scientists conduct research aimed at improving overall human health. They often use clinical trials and other investigative methods to reach their findings.  Design and conduct studies to investigate human diseases and methods to prevent and treat diseases Clinical pharmacologists
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Medical scientists typically have a Ph.D., usually in biology or a related life science. Some get a medical degree instead of, or in addition to, a Ph.D.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Medical scientists typically work in offices and laboratories. Most work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: medical scientists.    Agricultural and food scientists research ways to improve the efficiency and safety of agricultural establishments and products. Biochemists and biophysicists study the chemical and physical principles of living things and of biological processes. Epidemiologists are public health workers who investigate patterns and causes of disease and injury. Health education specialists develop programs to teach people about conditions affecting well-being. Clinical laboratory technologists and technicians perform medical laboratory tests for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease. Microbiologists study microorganisms such as bacteria, algae, and fungi. Physicians and surgeons diagnose and treat injuries or illnesses and address health maintenance. Postsecondary teachers instruct students in a variety of academic subjects beyond the high school level. Veterinarians care for the health of animals and work to protect public health. Biological technicians assist biological and medical scientists with tasks such as laboratory setup, data collection, and observation.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Medical transcriptionists, sometimes referred to as healthcare documentation specialists, use electronic devices to convert voice recordings from physicians and other healthcare workers into formal reports. Transcriptionists also may edit medical records for accuracy and return documents for review and approval.  Listen to the recorded dictation of a physician or other healthcare worker healthcare documentation specialists
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Medical transcriptionists typically need postsecondary education that leads to a certificate. Prospective medical transcriptionists must know basic medical terminology, anatomy and physiology, and rules of grammar. Some choose to become certified.   Computer skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Many medical transcriptionists work for hospitals, physicians' offices, and third-party transcription companies that provide services to healthcare establishments. Most are full time, but part-time work is common.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: medical transcriptionists.    Court reporters create word-for-word transcriptions at trials, depositions, and other legal proceedings. Simultaneous captioners provide similar transcriptions for television or for presentations in other settings, such as press conferences and business meetings, for people who are deaf or hard of hearing. Health information technologists and medical registrars advise organizations on computerized healthcare systems and analyze clinical data. Information clerks perform routine clerical duties, maintain records, collect data, and provide information to customers. Interpreters and translators convert information from one language into another language. Medical assistants complete administrative and clinical tasks, such as scheduling appointments and taking patients’ vital signs. Medical records specialists compile, process, and maintain patient files. Receptionists do tasks such as answering phones, receiving visitors, and providing information about their organization to the public. Secretaries and administrative assistants do routine clerical and organizational tasks.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Meeting, convention, and event planners arrange all aspects of events and professional gatherings. They arrange meeting locations, transportation, and other details.  Meet with clients to understand the purpose of the event Meeting planners
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Meeting, convention, and event planners typically need a bachelor’s degree. Some experience related to event planning may be helpful.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Meeting, convention, and event planners work in their offices and onsite at hotels or conference centers. They often travel to attend events and visit meeting sites. During meetings or conventions, planners may work many more hours than usual.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: meeting, convention, and event planners.    Administrative services and facilities managers plan, direct, and coordinate activities that help an organization run efficiently. Floral designers arrange live, dried, and silk flowers and greenery to make decorative displays. Food service managers are responsible for the daily operation of restaurants or other establishments that prepare and serve food and beverages. Fundraisers organize activities to raise money and other kinds of donations for an organization. Lodging managers ensure that guests have a pleasant experience at an accommodations facility. They also plan, direct, or coordinate activities to ensure that the facility is efficient and profitable. Travel agents sell transportation, lodging, and entertainment activities to individuals and groups planning trips.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Metal and plastic machine workers set up and operate equipment that cuts, shapes, and forms metal and plastic materials or pieces.  Set up and adjust machines according to blueprints Machine setters
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Metal and plastic workers typically need a high school diploma to enter the occupation and receive 1 year of on-the-job training. Computer numerically controlled (CNC) tool programmers typically need postsecondary education.   Computer skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Metal and plastic machine workers are employed mainly in factories. Workers must adhere to safety standards to protect themselves from workplace hazards. Most work full time, which for some includes evenings and weekends.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: metal and plastic machine workers.    Assemblers and fabricators build finished products and the parts that go into them. Computer programmers write, modify, and test code and scripts that allow computer software and applications to function properly. Industrial machinery mechanics, machinery maintenance workers, and millwrights install, maintain, and repair factory equipment and other industrial machinery. Machinists and tool and die makers set up and operate equipment to produce precision metal parts, instruments, and tools. Painting and coating workers apply finishes, often using machines, to a range of products.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Microbiologists study microorganisms such as bacteria, algae, and fungi. They investigate the growth, structure, and other characteristics of these organisms.  Plan and conduct research projects, such as improving sterilization procedures or developing drugs to combat infectious diseases Bacteriologists
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Microbiologists typically need a bachelor’s degree in microbiology or a related field to enter the occupation. Some employers prefer to hire candidates who have a master’s degree or Ph.D.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Microbiologists work in primarily in laboratories and offices. Most work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: microbiologists.    Agricultural and food scientists research ways to improve the efficiency and safety of agricultural establishments and products. Biochemists and biophysicists study the chemical and physical principles of living things and of biological processes. Biological technicians assist biological and medical scientists with tasks such as laboratory setup, data collection, and observation. Conservation scientists and foresters manage the land quality of forests, parks, rangelands, and other natural resources. Environmental scientists and specialists conduct research or investigations to protect the environment or human health. Geoscientists study the physical aspects of the Earth. Clinical laboratory technologists and technicians perform medical laboratory tests for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease. Medical scientists conduct research aimed at improving overall human health. Natural sciences managers plan, supervise, or coordinate research and other activities in fields such as life sciences, physical sciences, mathematics, and statistics. Zoologists and wildlife biologists study animals, those both in captivity and in the wild, and how they interact with their ecosystems.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Middle school teachers educate students, typically in sixth through eighth grade. Middle school teachers help students build on the fundamentals taught in elementary school and prepare students for high school.  Create lesson plans to teach students a subject English as a second language
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Middle school teachers typically need a bachelor’s degree. In addition, public school teachers must have a state-issued certification or license.  A bachelor’s degree with a minimum grade point average Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Middle school teachers work in public and private schools. They generally work during school hours when students are present and use nights and weekends to prepare lessons and grade papers. Most do not work during the summer.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: middle school teachers.    Career and technical education teachers instruct students in various technical and vocational subjects, such as auto repair, healthcare, and culinary arts. Childcare workers attend to children's needs while helping to foster early development. Elementary, middle, and high school principals oversee all school operations, including daily school activities. High school teachers teach academic lessons and various skills that students will need to attend college and to enter the job market. Instructional coordinators oversee school curriculums and teaching standards. They develop instructional material, implement it, and assess its effectiveness. Librarians and library media specialists help people find information and conduct research for personal and professional use. Postsecondary teachers instruct students in a variety of academic subjects beyond the high school level. Preschool teachers educate and care for children younger than age 5 who have not yet entered kindergarten. School counselors help students develop academic and social skills. Career counselors and advisors help people choose a path to employment. Social workers help people prevent and cope with problems in their everyday lives. Special education teachers work with students who have a wide range of learning, mental, emotional, and physical disabilities. Teacher assistants work with a licensed teacher to give students additional attention and instruction. Kindergarten and elementary school teachers instruct young students in basic subjects in order to prepare them for future schooling.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Members of the U.S. military service maintain the U.S. national defense. Although some service members work in occupations specific to the military, such as fighter pilots or infantrymen, many work in occupations that also exist in the civilian workplace, such as nurses, doctors, and lawyers. Members serve in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard, or in the Reserve components of these branches, and in the Air National Guard and Army National Guard. (The Coast Guard, which is included in this profile, is part of the Department of Homeland Security.)  Participate in, or support, military operations, such as combat or training operations, or humanitarian or disaster relief Enlisted personnel Occupational group Administrative Combat Specialty Construction Electronic and Electrical Equipment Repair Engineering, Science, and Technical Healthcare Human Resource Development Machine Operator and Production Media and Public Affairs Protective Service Support Service Transportation and Material Handling Vehicle and Machinery Mechanic Non-occupation or unspecified coded personnel Total enlisted personnel for each military branch and Coast Guard
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: To join the military, applicants must meet age, education, aptitude, physical, and character requirements. These requirements vary by branch of service and for officers and enlisted members.  Minimum of 17 years of age Leadership skills.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: The military employs people in numerous occupational specialties, many of which are similar to civilian occupations. To match military occupations with similar civilian occupations, O*Net OnLine offers the Military Crosswalk Search tool.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Mining and geological engineers design mines to safely and efficiently remove minerals such as coal and metals for use in manufacturing and utilities.  Design open-pit and underground mines Geological engineers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Mining and geological engineers, including a mining safety engineers, typically need a bachelor’s degree in engineering to enter the occupation.  A degree from an ABET-accredited engineering program Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Many mining and geological engineers work where mining operations are located, such as mineral mines or sand-and-gravel quarries, in remote areas or near cities and towns. Others work in offices or onsite for oil and gas extraction firms or engineering services firms.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: mining and geological engineers.    Architectural and engineering managers plan, direct, and coordinate activities in the fields of architecture and engineering. Civil engineers plan, design, and supervise the construction and maintenance of building and infrastructure projects. Environmental scientists and specialists conduct research or investigations to protect the environment or human health. Geological and hydrologic technicians support scientists and engineers in exploring, extracting, and monitoring natural resources. Geoscientists study the physical aspects of the Earth. Hydrologists study water and how it moves across and through the Earth’s crust. Mechanical engineers design, develop, build, and test mechanical and thermal sensors and devices. Petroleum engineers devise methods to improve oil and gas extraction and production. Sales engineers sell business products or services, such as software or support, that require technical expertise. Health and safety engineers apply their knowledge of industrial processes, mechanics, psychology, and other disciplines to promote worksite or product safety.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Models pose for artists, photographers, or customers to help advertise a variety of products, including clothing, cosmetics, food, and appliances. Models also work as a fit or fitting model, enabling the manufacturer or fashion designer to achieve the best fit for new styles.  Display clothing and merchandise in print and online advertisements
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: No formal education credential is required to become a model. Specific requirements depend on the client, with different jobs requiring different physical characteristics. However, most models must be within certain ranges for height, weight, and clothing size.   Discipline.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Models work in a variety of conditions, from comfortable indoor studios and runway fashion shows to outdoors in all weather conditions. Most models work part time and have unpredictable work schedules. Many also experience periods of unemployment.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: models.    Actors express ideas and portray characters in theater, film, television, and other performing arts media. Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists provide haircutting, hairstyling, and other services related to personal appearance. Fashion designers create clothing, accessories, and footwear. Photographers use their technical expertise, creativity, and composition skills to produce and preserve images.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Music directors, also called conductors, lead orchestras and other musical groups during performances and recording sessions. Composers write and arrange original music in a variety of musical styles.  Select musical arrangements and compositions to be performed for live audiences or recordings conductors
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Educational and training requirements for music directors and composers vary, although most positions require related work experience. A conductor for a symphony orchestra typically needs a master’s degree; a choir director may need a bachelor’s degree. There are no formal educational requirements for those interested in writing popular music.   Discipline.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most music directors work for religious organizations and schools, or are self-employed. Music directors may spend a lot of time traveling to different performances. Composers can work in offices, recording studios, or their own homes.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: music directors and composers.    Actors express ideas and portray characters in theater, film, television, and other performing arts media. Dancers and choreographers use dance performances to express ideas and stories. High school teachers teach academic lessons and various skills that students will need to attend college and to enter the job market. Kindergarten and elementary school teachers instruct young students in basic subjects in order to prepare them for future schooling. Middle school teachers educate students, typically in sixth through eighth grades. Musicians and singers play instruments or sing for live audiences and in recording studios. Postsecondary teachers instruct students in a variety of academic subjects beyond the high school level. Producers and directors make business and creative decisions about film, television, stage, and other productions. Writers and authors develop written content for various types of media.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Musicians and singers play instruments or sing for live audiences and in recording studios. They perform a variety of genres, such as classical, jazz, and rock.  Perform music for live audiences and recordings
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Musicians and singers typically do not need formal postsecondary education to enter the occupation. However, those pursuing careers in some genres, such as classical or opera, may choose to earn a bachelor’s or higher degree. Musicians and singers need extensive training and regular practice to acquire their skills.   Dedication.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Musicians and singers often perform in settings such as concert halls, churches, and clubs. Part-time work is common, and work schedules may vary and include mornings, nights, or weekends.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: musicians and singers.    Actors express ideas and portray characters in theater, film, television, and other performing arts media. Dancers and choreographers use dance performances to express ideas and stories. High school teachers teach academic lessons and various skills that students will need to attend college and to enter the job market. Kindergarten and elementary school teachers instruct young students in basic subjects in order to prepare them for future schooling. Middle school teachers educate students, typically in sixth through eighth grades. Music directors lead musical groups during performances and recording sessions. Composers write and arrange original music in a variety of musical styles. Postsecondary teachers instruct students in a variety of academic subjects beyond the high school level. Producers and directors make business and creative decisions about film, television, stage, and other productions.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Natural sciences managers plan, supervise, or coordinate activities in fields such as life sciences, physical sciences, mathematics, and statistics. They direct work related to research and development and coordinate activities such as testing, quality control, and production.  Set goals and strategies for researchers and product developers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Natural sciences managers typically need at least a bachelor’s degree in a natural science or related field. Most work as scientists before becoming managers.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Natural sciences managers work primarily in an office setting or in laboratories. Most work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: natural sciences managers.    Agricultural and food scientists research ways to improve the efficiency and safety of agricultural establishments and products. Architectural and engineering managers plan, direct, and coordinate activities in the fields of architecture and engineering. Biochemists and biophysicists study the chemical and physical principles of living things and of biological processes. Chemists and materials scientists research and analyze the chemical properties of substances to develop new materials, products, or knowledge. Environmental scientists and specialists conduct research or investigations to protect the environment or human health. Geoscientists study the physical aspects of the Earth. Medical scientists conduct research aimed at improving overall human health. Microbiologists study microorganisms such as bacteria, algae, and fungi. Physicists and astronomers study the interactions of matter and energy. Postsecondary teachers instruct students in a variety of academic subjects beyond the high school level.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Network and computer systems administrators install, configure, and maintain organizations’ local area networks (LANs), wide area networks (WANs), data communication networks, operating systems, and servers.  Determine an organization’s network and system needs and install operating and application hardware and software
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: To enter the occupation, network and computer systems administrators typically need a bachelor’s degree in a field related to computer or information science. Others may require a postsecondary certificate or an associate’s degree.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Network and computer systems administrators work for a variety of organizations, including computer systems design firms, schools, and financial institutions. Most work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week. Administrators may work evenings, nights, and weekends to monitor, maintain, or update networks and systems.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: network and computer systems administrators.    Computer and information systems managers plan, coordinate, and direct computer-related activities in an organization. Computer hardware engineers research, design, develop, and test computer systems and components. Computer network architects design and implement data communication networks, including local area networks (LANs), wide area networks (WANs), and intranets. Computer programmers write, modify, and test code and scripts that allow computer software and applications to function properly. Computer support specialists maintain computer networks and provide technical help to computer users. Computer systems analysts study an organization’s current computer systems and design ways to improve efficiency. Database administrators and architects create or organize systems to store and secure data. Information security analysts plan and carry out security measures to protect an organization’s computer networks and systems. Electrical engineers design, develop, test, and supervise the manufacture of electrical equipment. Software developers design computer applications or programs. Software quality assurance analysts and testers identify problems with applications or programs and report defects. Web developers create and maintain websites. Digital designers develop, create, and test website or interface layout, functions, and navigation for usability.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: News analysts, reporters, and journalists keep the public updated about current events and noteworthy information. They report international, national, and local news for newspapers, magazines, websites, television, and radio.  Research topics that an editor or news director has assigned to them multimedia journalists
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: News analysts, reporters, and journalists typically need a bachelor’s degree to enter the occupation. Internship or work experience on a college newspaper, radio station, or television station also may be helpful.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most news analysts, reporters, and journalists work for newspaper, website, or magazine publishers or in television or radio broadcasting. Others are self-employed. Most work full time, and their schedules vary.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: news analysts, reporters, and journalists.    Atmospheric scientists study, report on, and forecast the weather and climate. Broadcast, sound, and video technicians set up, operate, and maintain the electrical equipment for media programs. Editors plan, review, and revise content for publication. Film and video editors and camera operators manipulate moving images that entertain or inform an audience. Photographers use their technical expertise, creativity, and composition skills to produce and preserve images. Public relations managers direct the creation of materials that will enhance the public image of their employer or client. Fundraising managers coordinate campaigns that bring in donations for their organization. Public relations specialists create and maintain a positive public image for the clients they represent. Technical writers prepare instruction manuals, how-to guides, journal articles, and other supporting documents to communicate complex and technical information more easily. Writers and authors develop written content for various types of media.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Nuclear engineers research and develop projects or address problems concerning the release, control, and use of nuclear energy and nuclear waste disposal. Some of these engineers research new reactor designs. Others may specialize in the development of safety regulations related to the handling of nuclear materials or operation of nuclear power.  Design or develop nuclear equipment —such as reactor cores, nuclear batteries, and radiation shielding—and its associated instruments Defense.
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Nuclear engineers typically need at least bachelor’s degree in nuclear engineering or a related field of engineering.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Nuclear engineers typically work in office settings, but it may vary by employer. Most nuclear engineers work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: nuclear engineers.    Civil engineers plan, design, and supervise the construction and maintenance of building and infrastructure projects. Electrical and electronic engineering technologists and technicians help engineers design and develop equipment that is powered by electricity or electric current. Electrical engineers design, develop, test, and supervise the manufacture of electrical equipment. Health and safety engineers apply their knowledge of industrial processes, mechanics, psychology, and other disciplines to promote worksite or product safety. Mechanical engineers design, develop, build, and test mechanical and thermal sensors and devices. Physicists and astronomers study the interactions of matter and energy.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Nuclear medicine technologists prepare radioactive drugs and administer them to patients for imaging or treatment. They provide technical support to physicians or others who diagnose, care for, and treat patients and to researchers who investigate uses of radioactive drugs. They also may act as emergency responders in the event of a nuclear disaster.  Explain medical procedures to the patient and answer questions Nuclear cardiology technologists
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Nuclear medicine technologists typically need an associate’s degree from an accredited nuclear medicine technology program. Formal education programs in nuclear medicine technology or a related healthcare field lead to a certificate, an associate’s degree, or a bachelor’s degree. Most nuclear medicine technologists become certified, and some must be licensed.   Ability to use technology.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most nuclear medicine technologists work in hospitals. Some work in physicians’ offices, diagnostic laboratories, or imaging clinics. Most nuclear medicine technologists work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: nuclear medicine technologists.    Biological technicians assist biological and medical scientists with tasks such as laboratory setup, data collection, and observation. Diagnostic medical sonographers and cardiovascular technologists and technicians operate special equipment to create images or to conduct tests. Clinical laboratory technologists and technicians perform medical laboratory tests for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease. Medical dosimetrists calculate doses of radiation and design and oversee treatment plans for patients with cancer and other serious diseases. Nuclear technicians assist physicists, engineers, and other scientists in nuclear power generation and production activities, such as operating or maintaining nuclear testing equipment. Radiation therapists administer doses of radiation to patients who have cancer or other serious diseases. Radiologic technologists perform diagnostic imaging examinations on patients. MRI technologists operate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanners to create diagnostic images.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Nuclear technicians assist physicists, engineers, and other scientists in nuclear power generation and production activities. They may operate, maintain, or provide quality control for nuclear testing and research equipment and monitor radiation levels.  Monitor, test, and maintain equipment and systems used in nuclear power generation or laboratories
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Nuclear technicians typically need an associate’s degree in either nuclear science or a nuclear-related technology. Some enter the occupation with a high school diploma or postsecondary nondegree award plus experience, such as from the military or an apprenticeship. Once hired, nuclear technicians typically receive extensive on-the-job training.   Attention to detail.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Nuclear technicians typically work in nuclear power plants or in laboratories. Most work full-time. In power plants, their work schedules may vary to include nights, holidays, and weekends. Nuclear technicians must take precautions to avoid exposure to radiation.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: nuclear technicians.    Chemical technicians conduct laboratory tests to help scientists analyze the properties of materials. Hazardous materials removal workers identify and dispose of harmful substances such as asbestos, lead, and radioactive waste. Mechanical engineering technologists and technicians help mechanical engineers design, develop, test, and manufacture machines and other devices. Nuclear engineers research and develop projects or address problems concerning the release, control, and use of nuclear energy and nuclear waste disposal. Nuclear medicine technologists prepare and administer radioactive drugs for imaging or treatment. Power plant operators, distributors, and dispatchers control the systems that generate and distribute electric power. Occupational health and safety specialists and technicians collect data on, analyze, and design improvements to work environments and procedures. Environmental science and protection technicians monitor the environment and investigate sources of pollution and contamination, including those affecting public health.

/occupation/occupation_name_short_singul: Nurse Anesthetist, Nurse Midwife, or Nurse Practitioner
/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners, also referred to as advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs), coordinate patient care and may provide primary and specialty healthcare. The scope of practice varies from state to state.  Take and record patients' medical histories and symptoms advanced practice registered nurses
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners, also referred to as advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs), must have at least a master’s degree in their specialty role. APRNs also must be licensed registered nurses in their state, pass a national certification exam, and have a state APRN license.   advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs)
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners work in a variety of healthcare settings, including hospitals, physicians' offices, and clinics. Most advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs) work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners.    Audiologists diagnose, manage, and treat patients who have hearing, balance, or related problems. Occupational therapists evaluate and treat people who have injuries, illnesses, or disabilities to help them with vocational, daily living, and other skills that promote independence. Physical therapists help injured or ill people improve movement and manage pain. Physician assistants examine, diagnose, and treat patients under the supervision of a physician. Physicians and surgeons diagnose and treat injuries or illnesses and address health maintenance. Registered nurses (RNs) provide and coordinate patient care and educate patients and the public about various health conditions. Speech-language pathologists assess and treat people who have communication disorders.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Nursing assistants, sometimes called nursing aides, provide basic care and help patients with activities of daily living. Orderlies transport patients and clean treatment areas.  Clean and bathe patients nursing aides
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Nursing assistants typically must complete a state-approved education program and pass their state’s competency exam. Orderlies typically have at least a high school diploma or equivalent.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most nursing assistants and orderlies work in nursing and residential care facilities and in hospitals. They are physically active and may need to help lift or move patients.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: nursing assistants and orderlies.    Home health and personal care aides monitor the condition of people with disabilities or chronic illnesses and help them with daily living activities. Licensed practical nurses (LPNs) and licensed vocational nurses (LVNs) provide basic medical care. Medical assistants complete administrative and clinical tasks, such as scheduling appointments and taking patients’ vital signs. Occupational therapy assistants and aides help occupational therapists provide treatments and procedures to clients, or they do routine tasks such as preparing treatment rooms. Psychiatric technicians and aides care for people who have mental conditions or developmental disabilities. Physical therapist assistants and aides are supervised by physical therapists to help patients regain movement and manage pain after injuries and illnesses. Registered nurses (RNs) provide and coordinate patient care and educate patients and the public about various health conditions. Dental assistants provide patient care, take x rays, keep records, and schedule appointments. Veterinary assistants and laboratory animal caretakers handle routine animal care and help scientists,veterinarians, and others with their daily tasks.

/occupation/occupation_name_short_singul: Occupational Health and Safety Specialist or Technician
/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Occupational health and safety specialists and technicians collect data on, analyze, and design improvements to many types of work environments and procedures. Specialists inspect workplaces and enforce adherence to regulations on safety, health, and the environment. Technicians work with specialists to implement and evaluate programs aimed at mitigating risks to workers, property, the environment, and the public.  Inspect, test, and evaluate workplace environments, programs, equipment, and practices to ensure that they follow government safety regulations
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Occupational health and safety specialists typically need a bachelor’s degree in occupational health and safety or a related field. Technicians typically need at least a high school diploma to enter the occupation, and they receive training on the job. Some pursue professional certification.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Occupational health and safety specialists and technicians work in a variety of indoor or outdoor settings, such as offices and factories or construction sites. Their jobs may involve considerable travel and fieldwork. Most work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: occupational health and safety specialists and technicians.    Construction and building inspectors ensure that construction meets building codes and ordinances, zoning regulations, and contract specifications. Environmental scientists and specialists conduct research or investigations to protect the environment or human health. Health and safety engineers apply their knowledge of industrial processes, mechanics, psychology, and other disciplines to promote worksite or product safety. Environmental science and protection technicians monitor the environment and investigate sources of pollution and contamination, including those affecting public health.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Occupational therapists evaluate and treat people who have injuries, illnesses, or disabilities. They help clients meet goals to develop, recover, improve, and maintain skills needed for daily living and working.  Evaluate clients' conditions by reviewing their medical history, interviewing them, and observing them perform various tasks
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: To enter the occupation, occupational therapists typically need a master’s degree in occupational therapy. All states require occupational therapists to be licensed.   Adaptability.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Occupational therapists work in a variety of settings, such as hospitals, schools, and outpatient clinics. They stand for long periods and may need to lift or move clients.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: occupational therapists.    Occupational therapy assistants and aides help occupational therapists provide treatments and procedures to clients, or they do routine tasks such as preparing treatment rooms. Physical therapists help injured or ill people improve movement and manage pain. Recreational therapists plan, direct, and coordinate recreation-based medical treatment programs for people with disabilities, injuries, or illnesses. Speech-language pathologists assess and treat people who have communication disorders. Nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners coordinate patient care and may provide primary and specialty healthcare. Orthotists and prosthetists measure, design, fit, and adapt medical devices, such as supportive braces and artificial limbs, for patients who have disabling conditions. Physician assistants examine, diagnose, and treat patients under the supervision of a physician.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Occupational therapy assistants help occupational therapists provide treatments and procedures to clients. Occupational therapy aides do select or routine tasks, such as preparing treatment rooms, under the direction of occupational therapists or occupational therapy assistants.  Guide clients in therapeutic activities, such as exercises to improve motor skills and functional abilities  Occupational therapy assistants
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Occupational therapy assistants typically need an associate’s degree from an accredited occupational therapy assistant program. Occupational therapy assistants usually need a state-issued license. Occupational therapy aides typically need a high school diploma or equivalent and are trained on the job.   Adaptability.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Occupational therapy assistants and aides work primarily in occupational therapists’ offices, in hospitals, and in nursing care facilities. Occupational therapy assistants and aides spend much of their time standing while setting up equipment and, in the case of assistants, providing therapy to clients.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: occupational therapy assistants and aides.    Dental assistants provide patient care, take x rays, keep records, and schedule appointments. Home health and personal care aides monitor the condition of people with disabilities or chronic illnesses and help them with daily living activities. Medical assistants complete administrative and clinical tasks, such as scheduling appointments and taking patients’ vital signs. Nursing assistants provide basic care and help patients with activities of daily living. Orderlies transport patients and clean treatment areas. Occupational therapists evaluate and treat people who have injuries, illnesses, or disabilities to help them with vocational, daily living, and other skills that promote independence. Pharmacy technicians help pharmacists dispense prescription medication to customers or health professionals. Physical therapist assistants and aides are supervised by physical therapists to help patients regain movement and manage pain after injuries and illnesses. Psychiatric technicians and aides care for people who have mental conditions or developmental disabilities.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Operations research analysts use mathematics and logic to help organizations make informed decisions and solve problems.  Identify problems in areas such as business, logistics, healthcare, or other fields
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Operations research analysts typically need at least a bachelor’s degree to enter the occupation. Some employers require or prefer that applicants have a master’s degree. Analysts may need a degree in operations research or a related field, such as applied mathematics.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Operations research analysts spend much of their time in office settings, although travel may be necessary to meet with clients. Most operations research analysts work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: operations research analysts.    Data scientists use analytical tools and techniques to extract meaningful insights from data. Economists conduct research, prepare reports, and evaluate issues related to monetary and fiscal policy. They also may collect and analyze statistical data. Industrial engineers design, develop, and test integrated systems for managing industrial production processes. Logisticians analyze and coordinate an organization’s supply chain. Management analysts recommend ways to improve an organization’s efficiency. Market research analysts study consumer preferences, business conditions, and other factors to assess potential sales of a product or service. Mathematicians and statisticians analyze data and apply computational techniques to solve problems. Software developers design computer applications or programs. Software quality assurance analysts and testers identify problems with applications or programs and report defects.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Opticians fit customers for eyeglasses and contact lenses and help them select which frames and lenses to buy.  Receive customers’ prescriptions for eyeglasses or contact lenses
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Opticians typically need a high school diploma or the equivalent and receive on-the-job training. Some states require opticians to be licensed, which may include completing an associate’s degree or a certificate in ophthalmic dispensing or a related field.   Business skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Opticians work in a variety of settings. Some work in offices of optometrists or ophthalmologists. Others work in stores that sell eyeglasses, contact lenses, visual aids, and other optical goods.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: opticians.    Audiologists diagnose, manage, and treat patients who have hearing, balance, or related problems. Dental and ophthalmic laboratory technicians and medical appliance technicians make or repair dentures, eyeglasses, prosthetics, and related products. Jewelers and precious stone and metal workers design, construct, adjust, repair, appraise and sell jewelry and related products. Optometrists diagnose, manage, and treat conditions and diseases of the human eye and visual system, including examining eyes and prescribing corrective lenses. Orthotists and prosthetists measure, design, fit, and adapt medical devices, such as supportive braces and artificial limbs, for patients who have disabling conditions.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Optometrists diagnose, manage, and treat conditions and diseases of the human eye and visual system, including examining eyes and prescribing corrective lenses.  Perform vision tests and analyze results
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Optometrists typically need a Doctor of Optometry (O.D.) degree. O.D. programs take 4 years to complete, and applicants typically have bachelor’s degree before entering a program. Every state requires optometrist to be licensed.   Decision-making skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most optometrists work in offices or in optical goods stores. Optometrists usually work full time, but part-time work is common. Schedules may vary to include evenings and weekends.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: optometrists.    Chiropractors assess, treat, and care for patients by manipulating the spine and musculoskeletal system. Dentists diagnose and treat problems with patients’ teeth, gums, and related parts of the mouth. Opticians fit customers for eyeglasses and contact lenses and help them select which frames and lenses to buy. Physicians and surgeons diagnose and treat injuries or illnesses and address health maintenance. Podiatrists provide medical and surgical care for people with foot, ankle, and lower leg problems. Veterinarians care for the health of animals and work to protect public health. Audiologists diagnose, manage, and treat patients who have hearing, balance, or related problems. Dental and ophthalmic laboratory technicians and medical appliance technicians make or repair dentures, eyeglasses, prosthetics, and related products.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Orthotists and prosthetists measure, design, fit, and adapt musculoskeletal devices for patients who have disabling conditions. These devices include artificial limbs and orthopedic braces.  Evaluate and interview patients to determine their needs
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Orthotists and prosthetists typically need to complete a master's degree program and residency to enter the occupation. Some states require these workers to be licensed.   Compassion.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Orthotists and prosthetists usually work in healthcare settings and in laboratories. Most work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: orthotists and prosthetists.    Physical therapists help injured or ill people improve movement and manage pain. Physicians and surgeons diagnose and treat injuries or illnesses and address health maintenance. Respiratory therapists care for patients who have trouble breathing—for example, because of a chronic condition such as asthma. Dental and ophthalmic laboratory technicians and medical appliance technicians make or repair dentures, eyeglasses, prosthetics, and related products. Occupational therapists evaluate and treat people who have injuries, illnesses, or disabilities to help them with vocational, daily living, and other skills that promote independence.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Painters apply paint, stain, and coatings to walls and ceilings, buildings, large machinery and equipment, and bridges and other structures.  Protect floors, furniture, and trim by covering surfaces with drop cloths and tarps and securing with tape Commercial painters
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Painters typically learn their trade on the job. No formal education is typically required to enter the occupation.   Ability to work at heights.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Painters work indoors and outdoors. Painting is physically demanding and requires a lot of bending, kneeling, reaching, and climbing. Those who paint bridges or buildings may work at extreme heights or in uncomfortable positions.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: painters, construction and maintenance.    Carpenters construct, repair, and install building frameworks and structures made from wood and other materials. Construction laborers and helpers perform tasks, such as using, supplying, or holding materials or tools and cleaning work areas and equipment, on construction sites. Painting and coating workers apply finishes, often using machines, to a range of products. Drywall and ceiling tile installers hang wallboard and install ceiling tile inside buildings. Tapers prepare the wallboard for painting. Hazardous materials removal workers identify and dispose of harmful substances such as asbestos, lead, and radioactive waste. Flooring installers and tile and stone setters lay and finish carpet, wood, vinyl, tile, and other materials.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Painting and coating workers apply finishes, often using machines, to products such as cars, jewelry, and ceramics.  Set up and operate machines that paint or coat products Coating, painting, and spraying machine setters, operators, and tenders
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Painting and coating workers typically need a high school diploma or equivalent to enter the occupation. New workers usually train on the job for several months to attain competency.   Artistic ability.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most painting and coating workers are employed full time. They frequently stand for long periods in specially ventilated areas.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: painting and coating workers.    Automotive body and glass repairers restore, refinish, and replace vehicle bodies and frames, windshields, and window glass. Painters apply paint, stain, and coatings to walls and ceilings, buildings, large machinery and equipment, and bridges and other structures. Metal and plastic machine workers set up and operate equipment that cuts, shapes, and forms metal and plastic materials or pieces.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Paralegals and legal assistants support lawyers by performing a variety of tasks, such as maintaining and organizing files, conducting legal research, and drafting documents.  Investigate and gather the facts of a case
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Paralegals and legal assistants typically need an associate’s degree or certificate in paralegal studies to enter the occupation. Some employers prefer to hire candidates who have a bachelor’s degree; others may consider candidates who have a high school diploma and experience.   Communication skills.
