/occupation/summary_work_environment: Paralegals and legal assistants typically work in offices for a variety of employers, including law firms and government agencies. Most work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: paralegals and legal assistants.    Claims adjusters, appraisers, examiners, and investigators evaluate insurance claims. Lawyers advise and represent clients on legal proceedings or transactions. Secretaries and administrative assistants do routine clerical and organizational tasks. Arbitrators, mediators, and conciliators facilitate negotiation through dialogue to help resolve conflicts outside of the court system. Judges and hearing officers oversee legal matters in court or administrative proceedings.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Personal financial advisors provide advice on investments, insurance, mortgages, estate planning, taxes, and retirement to help individuals manage their finances.  Meet with clients to discuss their financial goals
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Personal financial advisors typically need a bachelor’s degree to enter the occupation. A master’s degree and certification may improve chances for advancement.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most personal financial advisors work in the finance and insurance industry or are self-employed. They typically work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week. They also may meet with clients in the evenings or on weekends.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: personal financial advisors.    Budget analysts help public and private organizations plan their finances. Financial analysts guide businesses and individuals in decisions about expending money to attain profit. Financial managers create financial reports, direct investment activities, and develop plans for the long-term financial goals of their organization. Insurance sales agents contact potential customers and sell one or more types of insurance. Insurance underwriters evaluate insurance applications and decide whether to approve them. Real estate brokers and sales agents help clients buy, sell, and rent properties. Securities, commodities, and financial services sales agents connect buyers and sellers in financial markets.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Pest control workers remove unwanted pests, such as roaches, rodents, ants, and termites, that infest buildings and surrounding areas.  Inspect buildings and premises for signs of pests or infestation Pest control technicians
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Pest control workers typically need a high school diploma and receive on-the-job training. State laws require pest control workers to be licensed.   Bookkeeping skills
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Pest control workers often kneel, bend, and crawl in tight spaces to inspect sites. Because there are health risks associated with pesticide use, workers are trained in pesticide safety and typically wear protective gear, which may include gloves, goggles, and respirators. Most pest control workers are employed full time. Working evenings and weekends is common.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: pest control workers.    Construction laborers and helpers perform tasks, such as using, supplying, or holding materials or tools and cleaning work areas and equipment, on construction sites. Grounds maintenance workers install and maintain landscapes, prune trees or shrubs, and do other tasks to ensure that vegetation is attractive, orderly, and safe. Janitors and building cleaners keep many types of buildings clean, sanitary, orderly, and in good condition.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Petroleum engineers devise methods to improve oil and gas extraction and production. They also oversee drilling and offer technical advice.  Design facilities to extract and produce oil and gas from reserves deep underground Completions engineers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Petroleum engineers typically need a bachelor’s degree in petroleum engineering or a related field, such as mechanical, civil, or chemical engineering. Employers also value practical experience, which students sometimes gain through internships.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Petroleum engineers generally work in offices or at drilling and well sites. Travel may be required to visit these sites or to meet with other engineers, oilfield workers, and customers.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: petroleum engineers.    Architectural and engineering managers plan, direct, and coordinate activities in the fields of architecture and engineering. Geoscientists study the physical aspects of the Earth. Industrial engineers design, develop, and test integrated systems for managing industrial production processes. Mechanical engineers design, develop, build, and test mechanical and thermal sensors and devices. Civil engineers plan, design, and supervise the construction and maintenance of building and infrastructure projects. Chemical engineers apply the principles of chemistry, physics, and engineering to design equipment and processes for manufacturing products such as gasoline, detergents, and paper. Mining and geological engineers design mines to safely and efficiently remove minerals for use in manufacturing and utilities. Geological and hydrologic technicians support scientists and engineers in exploring, extracting, and monitoring natural resources.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Pharmacists dispense prescription medications and provide information to patients about the drugs and their use. They also advise physicians and other healthcare workers on the selection, dosage, interactions, and side effects of medications to treat health problems. They may help patients with their overall health through activities such as providing immunizations.  Fill prescriptions to the proper amount based on physicians’ instructions Community pharmacists
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Pharmacists typically need a Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D.) degree from an accredited pharmacy program. Every state requires pharmacists to be licensed.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Pharmacists work in pharmacies, including those in drug, general merchandise, and grocery stores. They also work in hospitals and other healthcare facilities that are open 24 hours. Most pharmacists work full time, and some work nights, weekends, and holidays.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: pharmacists.    Biochemists and biophysicists study the chemical and physical principles of living things and of biological processes. Medical scientists conduct research aimed at improving overall human health. Pharmacy technicians help pharmacists dispense prescription medication to customers or health professionals. Physicians and surgeons diagnose and treat injuries or illnesses and address health maintenance. Registered nurses (RNs) provide and coordinate patient care and educate patients and the public about various health conditions.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Pharmacy technicians help pharmacists dispense prescription medication to customers or health professionals. They mainly work in retail pharmacies and hospitals.  Collect information needed to fill a prescription from customers or health professionals
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Pharmacy technicians usually need a high school diploma or equivalent and learn their duties through on-the-job training, or they may complete a postsecondary education program in pharmacy technology. Most states regulate pharmacy technicians, which is a process that may require passing an exam or completing a formal education or training program.  High school diploma or GED Customer-service skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Pharmacy technicians work in pharmacies, including those found in drug, general merchandise, and grocery stores, and in hospitals. Most work full time, but many work part time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: pharmacy technicians.    Dental assistants provide patient care, take x rays, keep records, and schedule appointments. Medical assistants complete administrative and clinical tasks, such as scheduling appointments and taking patients’ vital signs. Medical records specialists compile, process, and maintain patient files. Medical transcriptionists use electronic devices to convert voice recordings from physicians and other healthcare workers into formal reports. Pharmacists dispense prescription medications and provide information to patients about the drugs and their use.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Phlebotomists draw blood for purposes such as tests, research, or donations. They help patients or donors who are anxious before or have an adverse reaction after the blood draw.  Draw blood from patients or blood donors
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Phlebotomists typically enter the occupation with a certificate from a postsecondary phlebotomy program, but some qualify with a high school diploma and on-the-job training. Employers may prefer to hire candidates who have earned professional certification.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Phlebotomists are employed in a variety of settings, including hospitals, medical and diagnostic laboratories, blood donor centers, and doctors’ offices.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: phlebotomists.    Dental assistants provide patient care, take x rays, keep records, and schedule appointments. Clinical laboratory technologists and technicians perform medical laboratory tests for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease. Medical assistants complete administrative and clinical tasks, such as scheduling appointments and taking patients’ vital signs. Medical records specialists compile, process, and maintain patient files. Medical transcriptionists use electronic devices to convert voice recordings from physicians and other healthcare workers into formal reports. Veterinary assistants and laboratory animal caretakers handle routine animal care and help scientists,veterinarians, and others with their daily tasks. Veterinary technologists and technicians do medical tests that help diagnose animals’ injuries and illnesses.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Photographers use their technical expertise, creativity, and composition skills to produce and preserve images that tell a story or record an event.  Market or advertise services to attract clients Aerial photographers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Although portrait photographers are not required to have postsecondary education, many take classes because employers usually seek applicants with creativity and a "good eye," as well as a good technical understanding of photography. Photojournalists and industrial and scientific photographers often need a bachelor’s degree.  Be at least 16 years old Artistic ability.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Working conditions for photographers vary by specialty. Some photographers travel for photo shoots, working either indoors or outdoors. Others work in studios; still others work in laboratories and use microscopes to photograph subjects.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: photographers.    Architects plan and design houses, factories, office buildings, and other structures. Art directors are responsible for the visual style and images in magazines, newspapers, product packaging, and movie and television productions. Craft and fine artists use a variety of materials and techniques to create art for sale and exhibition. Desktop publishers use computer software to design page layouts for items that are printed or published online. Fashion designers create clothing, accessories, and footwear. Film and video editors and camera operators manipulate moving images that entertain or inform an audience. Graphic designers create visual concepts, using computer software or by hand, to communicate ideas that inspire, inform, and captivate consumers. Industrial designers combine art, business, and engineering to develop the concepts for manufactured products. Models pose for artists, photographers, and other clients to help advertise products. News analysts, reporters, and journalists keep the public updated about current events and noteworthy information.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Physical therapist assistants, sometimes called PTAs, and physical therapist aides work under the direction and supervision of physical therapists. They help patients who are recovering from injuries and illnesses to regain movement and manage pain.  Observe patients before, during, and after therapy, noting the patient’s status and reporting it to a physical therapist PTAs
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Physical therapist assistants entering the occupation typically need an associate’s degree from an accredited program and a license or certification. Physical therapist aides usually need a high school diploma or equivalent and on-the-job training.   Compassion.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most physical therapist assistants and aides work in physical therapists’ offices or in hospitals. They are frequently on their feet as they set up equipment and help care for patients.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: physical therapist assistants and aides.    Medical assistants complete administrative and clinical tasks, such as scheduling appointments and taking patients’ vital signs. Nursing assistants provide basic care and help patients with activities of daily living. Orderlies transport patients and clean treatment areas. Occupational therapy assistants and aides help occupational therapists provide treatments and procedures to clients, or they do routine tasks such as preparing treatment rooms. Pharmacy technicians help pharmacists dispense prescription medication to customers or health professionals. Physical therapists help injured or ill people improve movement and manage pain. Psychiatric technicians and aides care for people who have mental conditions or developmental disabilities. Dental assistants provide patient care, take x rays, keep records, and schedule appointments.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Physical therapists help injured or ill people improve movement and manage pain. They are often an important part of preventive care, rehabilitation, and treatment for patients with chronic conditions, illnesses, or injuries.  Review patients’ medical history and referrals or notes from doctors, surgeons, or other healthcare workers PTs
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Physical therapists entering the occupation need a Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) degree. All states require physical therapists to be licensed.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Physical therapists typically work in private offices and clinics, hospitals, patients’ homes, and nursing homes. They spend much of their time on their feet, actively working with patients.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: physical therapists.    Audiologists diagnose, manage, and treat patients who have hearing, balance, or related problems. Chiropractors assess, treat, and care for patients by manipulating the spine and musculoskeletal system. Occupational therapists evaluate and treat people who have injuries, illnesses, or disabilities to help them with vocational, daily living, and other skills that promote independence. Physical therapist assistants and aides are supervised by physical therapists to help patients regain movement and manage pain after injuries and illnesses. Recreational therapists plan, direct, and coordinate recreation-based medical treatment programs for people with disabilities, injuries, or illnesses. Speech-language pathologists assess and treat people who have communication disorders. Athletic trainers specialize in preventing, diagnosing, and treating muscle and bone injuries and illnesses. Exercise physiologists develop fitness and exercise programs to help people improve their health. Nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners coordinate patient care and may provide primary and specialty healthcare. Physician assistants examine, diagnose, and treat patients under the supervision of a physician. Orthotists and prosthetists measure, design, fit, and adapt medical devices, such as supportive braces and artificial limbs, for patients who have disabling conditions.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Physician assistants, also known as PAs, examine, diagnose, and treat patients under the supervision of a physician.  Obtain and review patients’ medical histories PAs
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Physician assistants typically need a master’s degree from an accredited educational program. Applicants to these programs typically have a bachelor's degree and experience caring directly for patients. All states require physician assistants to be licensed.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Physician assistants work in physicians’ offices, hospitals, outpatient clinics, and other healthcare settings. Most work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: physician assistants.    Emergency medical technicians (EMTs) and paramedics assess injuries and illnesses, provide emergency medical care, and may transport patients to medical facilities. Nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners coordinate patient care and may provide primary and specialty healthcare. Occupational therapists evaluate and treat people who have injuries, illnesses, or disabilities to help them with vocational, daily living, and other skills that promote independence. Physical therapists help injured or ill people improve movement and manage pain. Physicians and surgeons diagnose and treat injuries or illnesses and address health maintenance. Registered nurses (RNs) provide and coordinate patient care and educate patients and the public about various health conditions. Speech-language pathologists assess and treat people who have communication disorders.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Physicians and surgeons diagnose and treat injuries or illnesses and address health maintenance. Physicians examine patients; take medical histories; prescribe medications; and order, perform, and interpret diagnostic tests. They often counsel patients on diet, hygiene, and preventive healthcare. Surgeons operate on patients to treat injuries, such as broken bones; diseases, such as cancerous tumors; and deformities, such as cleft palates.  Take a patient’s medical history and perform a physical exam Anesthesiologists
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Physicians and surgeons typically need a bachelor’s degree as well as a degree from a medical school, which takes an additional 4 years to complete. Depending on their specialty, they also need 3 to 9 years in internship and residency programs. Subspecialization includes additional training in a fellowship of 1 to 3 years.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Physicians and surgeons work in both clinical and nonclinical settings. Clinical settings include physicians' offices and hospitals; nonclinical settings include government agencies, nonprofit organizations, and insurance companies.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: physicians and surgeons.    Chiropractors assess, treat, and care for patients by manipulating the spine and musculoskeletal system. Dentists diagnose and treat problems with patients’ teeth, gums, and related parts of the mouth. Nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners coordinate patient care and may provide primary and specialty healthcare. Optometrists diagnose, manage, and treat conditions and diseases of the human eye and visual system, including examining eyes and prescribing corrective lenses. Physician assistants examine, diagnose, and treat patients under the supervision of a physician. Podiatrists provide medical and surgical care for people with foot, ankle, and lower leg problems. Registered nurses (RNs) provide and coordinate patient care and educate patients and the public about various health conditions. Veterinarians care for the health of animals and work to protect public health.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Physicists and astronomers study the interactions of matter and energy. Theoretical physicists and astronomers may study the nature of time or the origin of the universe. Some physicists design and perform experiments with sophisticated equipment such as particle accelerators, electron microscopes, and lasers.  Develop scientific theories and models to explain the properties of the natural world, such as the force of gravity or the formation of subatomic particles Experimental physicists
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Physicists and astronomers typically need a Ph.D. for jobs in research and academia. However, physicist jobs in the federal government typically require a bachelor’s degree in physics.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Physicists and astronomers may work in offices, research laboratories, and observatories. Most physicists and astronomers work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: physicists and astronomers.    Biochemists and biophysicists study the chemical and physical principles of living things and of biological processes. Chemists and materials scientists research and analyze the chemical properties of substances to develop new materials, products, or knowledge. Computer and information research scientists design innovative uses for new and existing computing technology. Computer hardware engineers research, design, develop, and test computer systems and components. Electrical engineers design, develop, test, and supervise the manufacture of electrical equipment. Geoscientists study the physical aspects of the Earth. Materials engineers develop, process, and test materials used to create a wide range of products. Mathematicians and statisticians analyze data and apply computational techniques to solve problems. Medical dosimetrists calculate doses of radiation and design and oversee treatment plans for patients with cancer and other serious diseases. Nuclear engineers research and develop projects or address problems concerning the release, control, and use of nuclear energy and nuclear waste disposal. Postsecondary teachers instruct students in a variety of academic subjects beyond the high school level.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Plumbers, pipefitters, and steamfitters install and repair piping fixtures and systems.  Prepare cost estimates for clients Plumbers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Most plumbers, pipefitters, and steamfitters learn on the job through an apprenticeship. Some also attend vocational-technical school. Most states and some localities require plumbers to be licensed.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Plumbers, pipefitters, and steamfitters work in factories, homes, businesses, and other places where there are pipes and related systems. Plumbers are often on call for emergencies, so evening and weekend work is common.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: plumbers, pipefitters, and steamfitters.    Boilermakers assemble, install, maintain, and repair boilers, closed vats, and other large vessels or containers that hold liquids and gases. Construction and building inspectors ensure that construction meets building codes and ordinances, zoning regulations, and contract specifications. Construction laborers and helpers perform tasks, such as using, supplying, or holding materials or tools and cleaning work areas and equipment, on construction sites. Construction managers plan, coordinate, budget, and supervise construction projects from start to finish. Electricians install, maintain, and repair electrical power, communications, lighting, and control systems. General maintenance and repair workers fix and maintain machines, mechanical equipment, and buildings. Heating, air conditioning, and refrigeration mechanics and installers work on heating, ventilation, cooling, and refrigeration systems. Industrial machinery mechanics, machinery maintenance workers, and millwrights install, maintain, and repair factory equipment and other industrial machinery. Water transportation workers operate and maintain vessels that take cargo and people over water. Welders, cutters, solderers, and brazers use hand-held or remotely controlled equipment to join, repair, or cut metal parts and products.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Podiatrists diagnose illnesses, treat injuries, and perform surgery for people with foot, ankle, and lower leg problems.  Diagnose and assess patients’ conditions by reviewing medical histories, performing physical exams, and reviewing x rays and medical laboratory tests.
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Podiatrists must earn a Doctor of Podiatric Medicine (DPM) degree and complete a 3-year residency program. Every state requires podiatrists to be licensed.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Podiatrists usually work in offices of podiatry, other medical offices, or hospitals. Most work full time, and some need to be on call for emergencies.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: podiatrists.    Chiropractors assess, treat, and care for patients by manipulating the spine and musculoskeletal system. Occupational therapists evaluate and treat people who have injuries, illnesses, or disabilities to help them with vocational, daily living, and other skills that promote independence. Optometrists diagnose, manage, and treat conditions and diseases of the human eye and visual system, including examining eyes and prescribing corrective lenses. Orthotists and prosthetists measure, design, fit, and adapt medical devices, such as supportive braces and artificial limbs, for patients who have disabling conditions. Physical therapists help injured or ill people improve movement and manage pain. Physicians and surgeons diagnose and treat injuries or illnesses and address health maintenance. Dentists diagnose and treat problems with patients’ teeth, gums, and related parts of the mouth.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Police officers protect lives and property. Detectives and criminal investigators, who are sometimes called agents or special agents, gather facts and collect evidence of crimes.  Respond to emergency and nonemergency calls agents
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: The education typically required to enter the occupation ranges from a high school diploma to a college degree. Most police and detectives must graduate from their agency’s training academy before completing a period of on-the-job training. Other requirements vary, but candidates usually must be at least 21 years old and able to meet rigorous physical and personal qualifications. A felony conviction or drug use may disqualify a candidate.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Police and detective work can be physically demanding, stressful, and dangerous. Police and sheriff's patrol officers and transit and railroad police have some of the highest rates of injuries and illnesses of all occupations. Working around the clock in shifts is common.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: police and detectives.    Correctional officers guard people in penal institutions and guard those in transit between jail, courtroom, prison, or other point. Bailiffs are law enforcement officers who maintain order in courtrooms. Emergency medical technicians (EMTs) and paramedics assess injuries and illnesses, provide emergency medical care, and may transport patients to medical facilities. Firefighters control and put out fires and respond to emergencies involving life, property, or the environment. Private detectives and investigators gather, analyze, and report information to clients regarding legal or personal matters. Probation officers and correctional treatment specialists assist in rehabilitating law offenders in custody or on probation or parole. Security guards and gambling surveillance officers protect property from illegal activity. Emergency management directors prepare plans and procedures for responding to natural disasters or other emergencies. They also help lead the response during and after emergencies. Forensic science technicians aid criminal investigations by collecting and analyzing evidence. Fire inspectors detect fire hazards, recommend prevention measures, ensure compliance with state and local fire regulations, and investigate causes of fires.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Political scientists study the origin, development, and operation of political systems. They may research topics such as public opinion, political decision-making, and ideology. They also may analyze the structure of governments and political entities.  Research political subjects, such as the U.S. political system and foreign relations
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: To enter the occupation, political scientists typically need a master’s degree in political science, public administration, or a related field. However, some employers consider candidates who have a bachelor’s degree; others may prefer a Ph.D.   Adaptability.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most political scientists work full time in an office setting. They sometimes work additional hours.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: political scientists.    Anthropologists and archeologists study the origin, development, and behavior of humans. Economists conduct research, prepare reports, and evaluate issues related to monetary and fiscal policy. They also may collect and analyze statistical data. Market research analysts study consumer preferences, business conditions, and other factors to assess potential sales of a product or service. Postsecondary teachers instruct students in a variety of academic subjects beyond the high school level. Sociologists study society and social behavior by examining the groups, cultures, social institutions, and processes that develop when people interact and work together. Survey researchers design and conduct surveys and analyze data. Urban and regional planners develop comprehensive plans and programs for use of land and physical facilities in cities, counties, metropolitan areas, and other jurisdictions. Geographers study the Earth and the distribution of its land, features, and inhabitants. Historians research, analyze, interpret, and write about the past by studying historical documents and sources.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Postal service workers sell postage and related products and collect, sort, and deliver mail.  Collect letters and parcels Postal service clerks
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: To enter these occupations, postal service workers typically need no formal educational credential. However, job candidates must pass a written exam as part of the application process. The exam covers four areas: address cross comparison, forms completion, memory and coding, and personal characteristics and experience. For more information, contact the post office or mail processing center where you want to work.   Customer-service skills
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Postal service clerks and mail sorters, processors, and processing machine operators work indoors, typically in a post office. Mail carriers mostly work outdoors, delivering mail.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: postal service workers.    Customer service representatives interact with customers to handle complaints, process orders, and answer questions. Delivery truck drivers and driver/sales workers pick up, transport, and drop off packages and small shipments within a local region or urban area. Hand laborers and material movers manually move freight, stock, or other materials. Information clerks perform routine clerical duties, maintain records, collect data, and provide information to customers. Material recording clerks track product information in order to keep businesses and supply chains on schedule. Metal and plastic machine workers set up and operate equipment that cuts, shapes, and forms metal and plastic materials or pieces. Receptionists do tasks such as answering phones, receiving visitors, and providing information about their organization to the public. Retail sales workers sell merchandise, spare and replacement parts, and equipment to customers. Taxi drivers (including ride-hailing drivers), shuttle drivers, and chauffeurs transport people to and from the places they need to go. Tellers process routine transactions, such as cashing checks and depositing money, at a bank or credit union.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Postsecondary education administrators oversee student services, academics, and faculty research at colleges and universities. Their job duties vary depending on the department in which they work, such as admissions, student affairs, or the registrar’s office.  Determine how many students to admit to the school admissions
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Postsecondary education administrators typically need a master’s degree. However, there will be some opportunities for those with a bachelor’s degree. Employers typically prefer candidates who have experience working in a postsecondary academic administrative office, particularly for occupations such as registrars and academic deans.   Computer skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Postsecondary education administrators work for public and private schools. Most work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: postsecondary education administrators.    Administrative services and facilities managers plan, direct, and coordinate activities that help an organization run efficiently. Human resources managers plan, coordinate, and direct the administrative functions of an organization. Postsecondary teachers instruct students in a variety of academic subjects beyond the high school level. Public relations managers direct the creation of materials that will enhance the public image of their employer or client. Fundraising managers coordinate campaigns that bring in donations for their organization. Public relations specialists create and maintain a positive public image for the clients they represent. School counselors help students develop academic and social skills. Career counselors and advisors help people choose a path to employment. Top executives plan strategies and policies to ensure that an organization meets its goals. Training and development managers plan, coordinate, and direct skills- and knowledge-enhancement programs for an organization’s staff. Elementary, middle, and high school principals oversee all school operations, including daily school activities.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Postsecondary teachers instruct students in a variety of academic subjects beyond the high school level. They may also conduct research and publish scholarly papers and books.  Develop an instructional plan (known as a course outline or syllabus) for the course(s) they teach and ensure that it meets college and department standards professors
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Educational requirements vary with the subject taught and the type of educational institution. Typically, postsecondary teachers must have a Ph.D. or other doctoral degree in their field. However, a master's degree may be enough for some postsecondary teachers at community colleges. Other postsecondary teachers may need work experience in their field of expertise.   Critical-thinking skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most postsecondary teachers work in public and private colleges and universities, professional schools, and junior or community colleges. Most work full time, although part-time work is common.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: postsecondary teachers.    Career and technical education teachers instruct students in various technical and vocational subjects, such as auto repair, healthcare, and culinary arts. Elementary, middle, and high school principals oversee all school operations, including daily school activities. Instructional coordinators oversee school curriculums and teaching standards. They develop instructional material, implement it, and assess its effectiveness. Postsecondary education administrators oversee student services, academics, and faculty research at colleges and universities.

/occupation/occupation_name_short_singul: Power Plant Operator, Distributor, or Dispatcher
/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Power plant operators, distributors, and dispatchers control the systems that generate and distribute electric power.  Control power-generating, distribution, or transmission equipment Nuclear power reactor operators
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Power plant operators, distributors, and dispatchers typically need at least a high school diploma or the equivalent to enter the occupation. Employers may prefer to hire candidates who have experience. Once hired, power plant operators, distributors, and dispatchers typically receive extensive on-the-job training.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most power plant operators, distributors, and dispatchers work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week. They typically work rotating 8- or 12-hour shifts.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: power plant operators, distributors, and dispatchers.    Water and wastewater treatment plant and system operators manage a system of machines to transfer or treat water or wastewater. Stationary engineers and boiler operators control stationary engines, boilers, or other mechanical equipment. Construction equipment operators drive, maneuver, or control the heavy machinery used to construct roads, buildings, and other structures. Electricians install, maintain, and repair electrical power, communications, lighting, and control systems. Electrical and electronics installers and repairers install or repair a variety of electrical equipment. Electrical power-line installers and repairers install or repair cables or wires used in electrical power or distribution systems. Hazardous materials removal workers identify and dispose of harmful substances such as asbestos, lead, and radioactive waste. Nuclear technicians assist physicists, engineers, and other scientists in nuclear power generation and production activities, such as operating or maintaining nuclear testing equipment.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Preschool and childcare center directors supervise and lead staffs, design program plans, oversee daily activities, and prepare budgets. They are responsible for all aspects of their center’s program, which may include before- and after-school care.  Supervise preschool teachers and childcare workers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: A bachelor’s degree and experience in early childhood education are typically required to become a preschool or childcare center director. However, educational requirements vary. Additionally, some employers require these directors to have a nationally recognized credential, such as the Child Development Associate (CDA) credential.   Business skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Preschool and childcare center directors work primarily in child daycare services. Most work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: preschool and childcare center directors.    Childcare workers attend to children's needs while helping to foster early development. High school teachers teach academic lessons and various skills that students will need to attend college and to enter the job market. Kindergarten and elementary school teachers instruct young students in basic subjects in order to prepare them for future schooling. Middle school teachers educate students, typically in sixth through eighth grades. Preschool teachers educate and care for children younger than age 5 who have not yet entered kindergarten. Special education teachers work with students who have a wide range of learning, mental, emotional, and physical disabilities. Teacher assistants work with a licensed teacher to give students additional attention and instruction. Elementary, middle, and high school principals oversee all school operations, including daily school activities.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Preschool teachers educate and care for children younger than age 5 who have not yet entered kindergarten. They teach language, motor, and social skills to young children.  Teach children basic skills such as identifying colors, shapes, numbers, and letters
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Education and training requirements vary based on settings and state regulations. Preschool teachers typically need at least an associate’s degree.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Preschool teachers typically work in public and private schools or childcare centers. Many work the traditional 10-month school year, but some work year-round.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: preschool teachers.    Childcare workers attend to children's needs while helping to foster early development. High school teachers teach academic lessons and various skills that students will need to attend college and to enter the job market. Kindergarten and elementary school teachers instruct young students in basic subjects in order to prepare them for future schooling. Middle school teachers educate students, typically in sixth through eighth grades. Preschool and childcare center directors supervise and lead their staffs, design program plans, oversee daily activities, and prepare budgets. Special education teachers work with students who have a wide range of learning, mental, emotional, and physical disabilities. Teacher assistants work with a licensed teacher to give students additional attention and instruction.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Private detectives and investigators gather, analyze, and report information to clients regarding legal or personal matters. Their services include verifying people’s backgrounds, finding missing persons, and investigating crimes.  Interview people to gather information Skip tracers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Private detectives and investigators typically need at least a high school diploma or the equivalent and several years of work experience in a related occupation. Some employers prefer to hire candidates who have a college degree. Most states require private detectives and investigators to be licensed.   Attention to detail.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Private detectives’ and investigators’ work settings may depend on their assignment or case. For example, they may spend time in offices to research cases, or they may work in the field while doing surveillance. Most work full time, and schedules may vary to include early mornings, nights, and weekends.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: private detectives and investigators.    Accountants and auditors prepare and examine financial records. Bill and account collectors try to recover payment on overdue bills. Claims adjusters, appraisers, examiners, and investigators evaluate insurance claims. Financial examiners ensure compliance with laws that govern institutions handling monetary transactions. Security guards and gambling surveillance officers protect property from illegal activity. Paralegals and legal assistants supportlawyersby performing a variety of tasks, such as maintaining and organizing files, conducting legal research, and drafting documents. Fire inspectors detect fire hazards, recommend prevention measures, ensure compliance with state and local fire regulations, and investigate causes of fires. Police officers protect lives and property. Detectives and criminal investigators gather facts and collect evidence of possible crimes. Forensic science technicians aid criminal investigations by collecting and analyzing evidence.

/occupation/occupation_name_short_singul: Probation Officer or Correctional Treatment Specialist
/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Probation officers and correctional treatment specialists assist in rehabilitating law offenders in custody or on probation or parole.  Interview probationers and parolees, their friends, and their relatives in an office or at a residence to assess progress Probation officers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Probation officers and correctional treatment specialists typically need a bachelor’s degree. In addition, candidates may be required to pass competency exams, drug testing, and a criminal background check.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most probation officers and correctional treatment specialists work full time. Their jobs may involve traveling to meet with probationers and parolees. Working in high-crime areas or in institutions may be stressful and dangerous.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: probation officers and correctional treatment specialists.    Correctional officers guard people in penal institutions and guard those in transit between jail, courtroom, prison, or other point. Bailiffs are law enforcement officers who maintain order in courtrooms. Police officers protect lives and property. Detectives and criminal investigators gather facts and collect evidence of possible crimes. Social and human service assistants provide client services in a variety of fields, such as psychology, rehabilitation, and social work. Social workers help people prevent and cope with problems in their everyday lives. Substance abuse, behavioral disorder, and mental health counselors advise people on a range of issues, such as those relating to alcoholism, addictions, or depression.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Producers and directors make business and creative decisions about, film, television, stage, and other productions. They interpret a writer’s script to entertain, inform, or instruct an audience.  Select scripts or topics for a film, television, video, stage, or radio production Producers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Producers and directors typically have a bachelor’s degree. They also typically need several years of experience working on set in film, TV, stage, or other productions in positions such as actors, cinematographers, or film and video editors or in related occupations, such as theater managers.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Producers and directors are often under pressure to finish their work on time. Most producers and directors work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week. Their schedules may vary.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: producers and directors.    Actors express ideas and portray characters in theater, film, television, and other performing arts media. Art directors are responsible for the visual style and images in magazines, newspapers, product packaging, and movie and television productions. Dancers and choreographers use dance performances to express ideas and stories. Film and video editors and camera operators manipulate moving images that entertain or inform an audience. Special effects artists and animators create images that appear to move and visual effects for various forms of media and entertainment. Top executives plan strategies and policies to ensure that an organization meets its goals. Writers and authors develop written content for various types of media.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Project management specialists coordinate the budget, schedule, and other details of a project. They lead and guide the work of technical staff. Project management specialists also may serve as a point of contact for the client or customer.  Communicate with clients to determine project requirements and objectives
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Project management specialists typically need a bachelor’s degree that may be in a variety of fields, including business or project management. Although not always required, certification may be beneficial.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Project management specialists usually work in an office setting, but they occasionally travel to visit clients. Most work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: project management specialists.    Cost estimators collect and analyze data in order to assess the time, money, materials, and labor required to make a product or provide a service. Logisticians analyze and coordinate an organization’s supply chain. Management analysts recommend ways to improve an organization’s efficiency. Market research analysts study consumer preferences, business conditions, and other factors to assess potential sales of a product or service. Mathematicians and statisticians analyze data and apply computational techniques to solve problems. Operations research analysts use mathematics and logic to help solve complex issues. Survey researchers design and conduct surveys and analyze data.

/occupation/occupation_name_short_singul: Property, Real Estate, or Community Association Manager
/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Property, real estate, and community association managers oversee many aspects of residential, commercial, or industrial properties. They ensure that the property is well maintained, has a nice appearance, operates smoothly, and preserves its resale value.  Meet with prospective tenants or owners and show them properties Property and real estate managers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Property, real estate, and community association managers typically need a high school diploma combined with several years of related work experience for entry-level positions. Some managers also must have a state-issued license.   Communication skills
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most property, real estate, and community association managers work full time. They usually work in an office setting but may spend part of their workday on tasks away from the office, such as showing apartments, inspecting the grounds, or meeting with owners.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: property, real estate, and community association managers.    Administrative services and facilities managers plan, direct, and coordinate activities that help an organization run efficiently. Food service managers are responsible for the daily operation of restaurants or other establishments that prepare and serve food and beverages. Lodging managers ensure that guests have a pleasant experience at an accommodations facility. They also plan, direct, or coordinate activities to ensure that the facility is efficient and profitable. Real estate brokers and sales agents help clients buy, sell, and rent properties.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Property appraisers and assessors provide a value estimate on real estate and tangible personal and business property.  Verify descriptions of property, such as by consulting public records Appraisers of personal and business property
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: The requirements to become a fully qualified property appraiser or assessor are complex and vary by state and, sometimes, by the value or type of property. These workers typically need a bachelor’s degree, although some qualify with a high school diploma. Appraisers of real estate also must meet state licensure or certification requirements. Check with your state's licensing board for specific requirements.   Analytical skills
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Although property appraisers and assessors work in offices, they may spend a large part of their time conducting site visits. Most work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: property appraisers and assessors.    Claims adjusters, appraisers, examiners, and investigators evaluate insurance claims. Construction and building inspectors ensure that construction meets building codes and ordinances, zoning regulations, and contract specifications. Real estate brokers and sales agents help clients buy, sell, and rent properties.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Psychiatric technicians and aides care for people who have mental or emotional conditions or developmental disabilities. Technicians typically monitor patients’ conditions and provide therapeutic care, such as overseeing their medications. Aides help patients in their daily activities and ensure a safe and clean environment.  Listen to patients' concerns, observe their behavior, and record their condition
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: To enter the occupation, psychiatric technicians typically need a postsecondary certificate, and aides need at least a high school diploma or equivalent. Some states require technicians to be licensed. Both technicians and aides get on-the-job training.   Compassion.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Psychiatric technicians and aides work primarily in healthcare settings, such as psychiatric hospitals and residential mental health facilities. The work may be physically demanding, and technicians and aides risk injury on the job. Most are full time, but part-time work is common; schedules may include nights, weekends, or holidays in facilities that are open 24 hours.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: psychiatric technicians and aides.    Childcare workers attend to children's needs while helping to foster early development. Home health and personal care aides monitor the condition of people with disabilities or chronic illnesses and help them with daily living activities. Licensed practical nurses (LPNs) and licensed vocational nurses (LVNs) provide basic medical care. Medical assistants complete administrative and clinical tasks, such as scheduling appointments and taking patients’ vital signs. Nursing assistants provide basic care and help patients with activities of daily living. Orderlies transport patients and clean treatment areas. Occupational therapy assistants and aides help occupational therapists provide treatments and procedures to clients, or they do routine tasks such as preparing treatment rooms. Registered nurses (RNs) provide and coordinate patient care and educate patients and the public about various health conditions. Social and human service assistants provide client services in a variety of fields, such as psychology, rehabilitation, and social work.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Psychologists study cognitive, emotional, and social processes and behavior by observing, interpreting, and recording how people relate to one another and to their environments. They use their findings to help improve processes and behaviors.  Study behavior and brain function by observing, interviewing, and surveying individuals Clinical and counseling psychologists
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Psychologists typically need an advanced degree, such as a master’s or doctoral degree, in psychology. Licensing requirements vary by state and position.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Psychologists work in a variety of settings, such as schools, hospitals, and private practice. Most are full time, but part-time work is common. Some work evenings or weekends to accommodate their clients' schedules.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: psychologists.    Market research analysts study consumer preferences, business conditions, and other factors to assess potential sales of a product or service. Marriage and family therapists diagnose and treat cognitive, behavioral, or similar disorders in the context of couples and other relationships. Physicians and surgeons diagnose and treat injuries or illnesses and address health maintenance. Postsecondary teachers instruct students in a variety of academic subjects beyond the high school level. School counselors help students develop academic and social skills. Career counselors and advisors help people choose a path to employment. Social workers help people prevent and cope with problems in their everyday lives. Sociologists study society and social behavior by examining the groups, cultures, social institutions, and processes that develop when people interact and work together. Substance abuse, behavioral disorder, and mental health counselors advise people on a range of issues, such as those relating to alcoholism, addictions, or depression. Survey researchers design and conduct surveys and analyze data. Training and development specialists plan and administer programs that improve the skills and knowledge of their employees.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Public relations managers plan and direct the creation of material that will enhance the public image of their employer or client. Fundraising managers coordinate campaigns that bring in donations for their organization.  Develop their organization’s or client’s corporate image and identity Public relations managers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Public relations and fundraising managers typically need at least a bachelor’s degree, and some positions may require a master’s degree. Many years of related work experience are also necessary.   Interpersonal skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Public relations and fundraising managers generally work in offices during regular business hours. However, many of these managers travel to give speeches and to attend meetings and community activities. Some work more than 40 hours per week.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: public relations and fundraising managers.    Advertising sales agents sell promotional space to businesses and individuals. Advertising, promotions, and marketing managers plan programs to generate interest in products or services. Fundraisers organize activities to raise money and other kinds of donations for an organization. Market research analysts study consumer preferences, business conditions, and other factors to assess potential sales of a product or service. Special effects artists and animators create images that appear to move and visual effects for various forms of media and entertainment. Public relations specialists create and maintain a positive public image for the clients they represent.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Public relations specialists create and maintain a positive public image for the individuals, groups, or organizations they represent. They craft media releases and develop social media programs to shape public perception of their clients and to increase awareness of each client’s work and goals.  Write press releases and prepare information for the media communications specialists
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Public relations specialists typically need a bachelor’s degree to enter the occupation. Employers may prefer to hire candidates who have studied a particular field, such as communications or business.   Interpersonal skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Public relations specialists work for a variety of organizations, including schools, media buyers, and professional associations. They usually work in offices, but they also deliver speeches, attend meetings and community activities, and occasionally travel.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: public relations specialists.    Advertising, promotions, and marketing managers plan programs to generate interest in products or services. Writers and authors develop written content for various types of media.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Public safety telecommunicators, including 911 operators and fire dispatchers, answer emergency and nonemergency calls and provide resources to assist those in need.  Answer 9-1-1 emergency and nonemergency requests from different sources, such as phone calls, text messages, social media, and alarm systems 911 operators
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Public safety telecommunicators typically need a high school diploma to enter the occupation and then are trained on the job. Many states and localities require these workers to become certified.   Ability to multitask.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Public safety telecommunicators work in emergency communication centers called public safety answering points (PSAPs). These workers usually have shifts that include evenings, weekends, and holidays to provide round-the-clock coverage. The pressure to respond quickly and calmly in alarming situations may be stressful.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: public safety telecommunicators.    Air traffic controllers coordinate the movement of aircraft to maintain safe distances between them. Customer service representatives interact with customers to handle complaints, process orders, and answer questions. Emergency medical technicians (EMTs) and paramedics assess injuries and illnesses, provide emergency medical care, and may transport patients to medical facilities. Power plant operators, distributors, and dispatchers control the systems that generate and distribute electric power. Security guards and gambling surveillance officers protect property from illegal activity.

/occupation/occupation_name_short_singul: Purchasing Manager, Buyer, or Purchasing Agent
/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Buyers and purchasing agents buy products and services for organizations to use or resell. They evaluate suppliers, negotiate contracts, and review the quality of products. Purchasing managers oversee the work of buyers and purchasing agents and typically handle more complex procurement tasks.  Evaluate suppliers on the basis of the price, quality, and speed of delivery of their products and services Purchasing agents and buyers of farm products
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Purchasing managers, buyers, and purchasing agents typically need a bachelor’s degree, although some employers hire candidates who have a high school diploma. Purchasing managers also need several years of related work experience.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Purchasing managers and buyers and purchasing agents usually work in an office setting. Most work full time. Travel may be required.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: purchasing managers, buyers, and purchasing agents.    Advertising, promotions, and marketing managers plan programs to generate interest in products or services. Bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks compute, classify, and record data to help organizations keep complete and accurate financial records. Financial clerks do administrative work, help customers, and carry out transactions that involve money. Financial managers create financial reports, direct investment activities, and develop plans for the long-term financial goals of their organization. Food service managers are responsible for the daily operation of restaurants or other establishments that prepare and serve food and beverages. Lodging managers ensure that guests have a pleasant experience at an accommodations facility. They also plan, direct, or coordinate activities to ensure that the facility is efficient and profitable. Logisticians analyze and coordinate an organization’s supply chain. Material recording clerks track product information in order to keep businesses and supply chains on schedule. Transportation, storage, and distribution managers plan, direct, or coordinate the movement of people and goods. Wholesale and manufacturing sales representatives sell goods for wholesalers or manufacturers to businesses, government agencies, and other organizations.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Quality control inspectors examine products and materials for defects or deviations from specifications.  Read blueprints and specifications Materials inspectors
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Quality control inspectors typically need a high school diploma to enter the occupation and receive on-the-job training once employed.   Detail oriented.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Many quality control inspectors work in manufacturing. Most work full time, and overtime may be required to meet production deadlines.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: quality control inspectors.    Construction and building inspectors ensure that construction meets building codes and ordinances, zoning regulations, and contract specifications. Fire inspectors detect fire hazards, recommend prevention measures, ensure compliance with state and local fire regulations, and investigate causes of fires. Industrial engineers design, develop, and test integrated systems for managing industrial production processes. Industrial engineering technologists and technicians help engineers solve problems affecting manufacturing layout or production. Logisticians analyze and coordinate an organization’s supply chain.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Radiation therapists administer doses of radiation to patients who have cancer or other serious diseases.  Explain treatment plans to the patient and answer questions about treatment
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Radiation therapists typically need an associate’s or bachelor’s degree in radiation therapy. Most states require radiation therapists to be licensed or certified, which often includes passing a national certification exam.   Compassion.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Radiation therapists work in hospitals, offices of physicians, and outpatient centers. Most radiation therapists work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: radiation therapists.    Dental hygienists examine patients for signs of oral diseases, such as gingivitis, and provide preventive care, including oral hygiene. Diagnostic medical sonographers and cardiovascular technologists and technicians operate special equipment to create images or to conduct tests. Medical dosimetrists calculate doses of radiation and design and oversee treatment plans for patients with cancer and other serious diseases. Nuclear medicine technologists prepare and administer radioactive drugs for imaging or treatment. Nursing assistants provide basic care and help patients with activities of daily living. Orderlies transport patients and clean treatment areas. Physical therapist assistants and aides are supervised by physical therapists to help patients regain movement and manage pain after injuries and illnesses. Radiologic technologists perform diagnostic imaging examinations on patients. MRI technologists operate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanners to create diagnostic images. Registered nurses (RNs) provide and coordinate patient care and educate patients and the public about various health conditions. Respiratory therapists care for patients who have trouble breathing—for example, because of a chronic condition such as asthma.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Radiologic technologists, also known as radiographers, perform x rays and other diagnostic imaging examinations on patients. MRI technologists operate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanners to create diagnostic images.  Adjust and maintain imaging equipment radiographers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Radiologic technologists and MRI technologists typically need an associate’s degree. MRI technologists may start out as radiologic technologists. Most states require radiologic technologists to be licensed or certified, but few states require licensure for MRI technologists. Regardless of state requirements, employers typically require or prefer to hire technologists who are certified.   Detail oriented.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Radiologic and MRI technologists work in healthcare facilities, and more than half work in hospitals. Most radiologic and MRI technologists work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: radiologic and MRI technologists.    Diagnostic medical sonographers and cardiovascular technologists and technicians operate special equipment to create images or to conduct tests. Medical dosimetrists calculate doses of radiation and design and oversee treatment plans for patients with cancer and other serious diseases. Nuclear medicine technologists prepare and administer radioactive drugs for imaging or treatment. Radiation therapists administer doses of radiation to patients who have cancer or other serious diseases. Veterinary technologists and technicians do medical tests that help diagnose animals’ injuries and illnesses.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Railroad workers ensure that passenger and freight trains run on time and travel safely. Some workers drive trains, some coordinate the activities of the trains, and others operate signals and switches in the rail yard.  Check the mechanical condition of locomotives and make adjustments when necessary Conductors
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Workers in railroad occupations typically need a high school diploma or equivalent and several months of on-the-job training.   Communication skills
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Nearly all railroad workers are employed in the rail transportation industry. Most work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: railroad workers.    Bus drivers transport people between various places. Delivery truck drivers and driver/sales workers pick up, transport, and drop off packages and small shipments within a local region or urban area. Heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers transport goods from one location to another. Material moving machine operators use equipment to transport objects. Water transportation workers operate and maintain vessels that take cargo and people over water.

/occupation/occupation_name_short_singul: Real Estate Broker or Sales Agent
/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Real estate brokers and sales agents help clients buy, sell, and rent properties. Although brokers and agents do similar work, brokers are licensed to manage their own real estate businesses. Sales agents must work with a real estate broker.  Solicit potential clients to buy, sell, and rent properties Real estate brokers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Real estate brokers and sales agents typically need a high school diploma or equivalent to enter the occupation. They also must complete a number of real estate courses and pass a licensing exam. States typically require licensed agents to have experience before obtaining a broker’s license.   Business skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Most real estate brokers and sales agents are self-employed. Although they often work irregular hours, many are able to set their own schedules.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: real estate brokers and sales agents.    Advertising sales agents sell promotional space to businesses and individuals. Property appraisers and assessors provide a value estimate on real estate and on tangible personal and business property. Insurance sales agents contact potential customers and sell one or more types of insurance. Loan officers evaluate, authorize, or recommend approval of loan applications. Property, real estate, and community association managers oversee many aspects of residential, commercial, or industrial properties. Securities, commodities, and financial services sales agents connect buyers and sellers in financial markets. Wholesale and manufacturing sales representatives sell goods for wholesalers or manufacturers to businesses, government agencies, and other organizations. Retail sales workers sell merchandise, spare and replacement parts, and equipment to customers. Personal financial advisors provide advice to help individuals manage their money and plan for their financial future.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Receptionists do administrative tasks, such as answering phones, greeting visitors, and providing general information about their organization.  Answer the telephone and take messages or forward calls
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Although hiring requirements vary by industry and employer, receptionists typically need a high school diploma or equivalent and good communication skills.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Receptionists are employed in nearly every industry.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: receptionists.    Customer service representatives interact with customers to handle complaints, process orders, and answer questions. General office clerks perform a variety of clerical tasks, including answering telephones, typing documents, and filing records. Information clerks perform routine clerical duties, maintain records, collect data, and provide information to customers. Library technicians and assistants help librarians with all aspects of running a library. Secretaries and administrative assistants do routine clerical and organizational tasks. Tellers process routine transactions, such as cashing checks and depositing money, at a bank or credit union.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Recreational therapists plan, direct, and coordinate recreation-based medical treatment programs to help maintain or improve patients’ physical, social, and emotional well-being. These therapists use a variety of techniques, including art expression; drama, music, and dance; sports and games; aquatics; and community outings.  Assess patients’ needs through observation, medical records, tests, and discussions with other healthcare workers and patients and their families
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Recreational therapists typically need a bachelor’s degree to enter the occupation. Employers may require or prefer therapists to be certified.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Recreational therapists work in a variety of settings, including hospitals, nursing homes, and government parks and recreation departments. Most work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: recreational therapists.    Occupational therapists evaluate and treat people who have injuries, illnesses, or disabilities to help them with vocational, daily living, and other skills that promote independence. Physical therapists help injured or ill people improve movement and manage pain. Rehabilitation counselors work with clients to overcome or manage the personal, social, or psychological effects of disabilities on employment or independent living. School counselors help students develop academic and social skills. Career counselors and advisors help people choose a path to employment. Speech-language pathologists assess and treat people who have communication disorders. Special education teachers work with students who have a wide range of learning, mental, emotional, and physical disabilities. Athletic trainers specialize in preventing, diagnosing, and treating muscle and bone injuries and illnesses. Exercise physiologists develop fitness and exercise programs to help people improve their health. Social workers help people prevent and cope with problems in their everyday lives.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Recreation workers organize, conduct, and promote a variety of group activities for leisure and other purposes. Activities may include arts and crafts, sports, or music.  Organize, conduct, and promote recreational activities camp counselors
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Recreation workers typically need at least a high school diploma or the equivalent, although requirements may vary by type of job. Once hired, these workers typically need a short period of on-the-job training.   Communication skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Recreation workers are employed in a variety of settings, including recreation centers, parks, and summer camps. Most work full time, but many work part-time, irregular, or seasonal hours.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: recreation workers.    Athletic trainers specialize in preventing, diagnosing, and treating muscle and bone injuries and illnesses. /occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Registered nurses usually take one of three education paths: a bachelor’s degree in nursing, an associate’s degree in nursing, or a diploma from an approved nursing program. Registered nurses must be licensed.   Critical-thinking skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Registered nurses work in hospitals, physicians’ offices, home healthcare services, and nursing care facilities. Others work in outpatient clinics and schools.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: registered nurses.    Dental hygienists examine patients for signs of oral diseases, such as gingivitis, and provide preventive care, including oral hygiene. Respiratory therapists care for patients who have trouble breathing—for example, because of a chronic condition such as asthma.

/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Respiratory therapists typically need an associate’s degree in respiratory therapy. Some employers prefer to hire candidates who have a bachelor’s degree. /occupation/summary_work_environment: Most respiratory therapists work full time. Because they may work in medical facilities that are always open, such as hospitals, they may have shifts that include nights, weekends, or holidays.

/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: Retail sales workers typically do not need formal education to enter the occupation. However, some employers prefer to hire candidates who have a high school diploma or the equivalent. Most retail sales workers learn on the job.   Customer-service skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Retail sales workers usually work in clean, well-lit stores. Most are employed full time. Schedules may vary, with evening and weekend work required in some jobs.

/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: There are no specific education requirements for roofers. Although most learn on the job, some roofers enter the occupation through an apprenticeship.   Ability to work at heights.

Insulation workers install and replace the materials used to insulate buildings or mechanical systems. Masonry workers use bricks, concrete and concrete blocks, and natural and manmade stones to build structures. Sheet metal workers fabricate or install products that are made from thin metal sheets. Solar photovoltaic (PV) installers assemble, set up, and maintain rooftop or other systems that convert sunlight into energy.

/occupation/what_they_do/section_body: Sales engineers sell business products or services, such as software or support, that require technical expertise.  Prepare and deliver presentations explaining technical products to existing and prospective customers
/occupation/how_to_become_one/section_bo: To enter the occupation, sales engineers typically need a bachelor’s degree. They combine technical knowledge of the products or services they sell with strong interpersonal skills.   Analytical skills.
/occupation/summary_work_environment: Sales engineers typically work in an office setting and often travel to meet with customers. Most sales engineers work full time.
/occupation/similar_occupations/section_: sales engineers.    Aerospace engineers design, develop, and test aircraft, spacecraft, satellites, and missiles.
